problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨4-2{t}^{2},1-3{t}^{3}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}+5,\,6+{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=3.$ Do not round the answers.

$a(3)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}+5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6+{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2}-4t,\,3{t}^{2}-8t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-8t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6t-4,\,6t-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=3,$ we substitute $t=3$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(3) & =⟨6(3)-4,\,6(3)-8⟩ \\  & =⟨14,\,10⟩\end{aligned}
$$
